identity.name: Ascorbyl palmitate
identity.chemical_class: Fatty-acid ester of ascorbic acid (lipophilic antioxidant)

function.mechanism: Acts as a lipid-phase antioxidant and is assumed to be rapidly hydrolysed pre-systemically to ascorbic acid and palmitate.
common_food_categories: Foods for special medical purposes for infants (EU FC 13.1.5.1)

adi.basis: EFSA 2020 follow-up states ANS (2015) found data too limited to establish a specific ADI for ascorbyl palmitate; historical JECFA temporary ADI 1.25 mg/kg bw/day is discussed in EFSA text.

efsa.key_finding: At MPLs in infant formula/infant FSMP, intake of hydrolysis products (ascorbic acid and palmitate) does not raise safety concerns; EFSA recommended specification updates.

adi.basis: Latest JECFA evaluation (2025) lists group ADI 'not specified' and withdraws previous 0-1.25 mg/kg bw/day.

concerns.summary: EFSA reports additive-specific toxicological data were too limited to set a stand-alone ADI for ascorbyl palmitate in prior re-evaluation; clinical infant-formula studies were not designed to isolate ascorbyl palmitate effects and had design limitations.
Historical exposure scenarios can exceed historical temporary ADI benchmarks (0-1.25 mg/kg bw/day), especially in infant FSMP and brand-loyal child scenarios.
key_references: EFSA Journal 2020 full text discussion of prior ANS/JECFA context

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2020: intake of metabolites at MPLs in infant formula and infant FSMP does not raise safety concerns.
JECFA 2025: rapid/extensive pre-systemic hydrolysis and low systemic exposure supported a group ADI not specified.
eCFR: GRAS status in 21 CFR 182.3149 under GMP conditions.

populations: Infants below 16 weeks consuming FSMP at high-level scenarios
Children in historical brand-loyal high-percentile exposure scenarios
adi_exceedance.notes: Exceedance refers to historical temporary ADI benchmarks (0-1.25 mg/kg bw/day). Current JECFA position is ADI not specified, and EFSA 2020 did not identify safety concern at assessed MPL scenarios.

risk_assessment.rationale: Major regulators continue to permit use; EFSA and JECFA emphasize hydrolysis to common metabolites and report no safety concern at assessed uses. Residual uncertainty remains because additive-specific toxicology and controlled human data are limited.
key_factors: EFSA 2020 no-safety-concern conclusion for infant formula contexts
JECFA 2025 ADI transition to 'not specified' with withdrawal of prior temporary ADI
Documented data gaps and high-exposure scenarios in some subpopulations
